messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Alert — GPU pool us-west2-spot reporting sustained capacity exhaustion and queue growth >100k. Autoscaler errors seen. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/1998765432

sre_oncall_jess: saw it. Paging now. Bridging 10m. anyone on-call for runtime?

runtime_maria: i'm up, jumping in. quick summary?

sre_oncall_jess: queue length spiked from 2k -> 120k over last 6m. Many requests throttled (HTTP 429) and some 503s for heavy-gen routes. Autoscaler is failing to procure spot GPUs — cloud returns InsufficientCapacity.

eng_kevin: confirmed in autoscaler logs: "RequestInstances failed: InsufficientInstanceCapacity: Not enough spot capacity available" and also a 403 from quota API intermittently. paste logs:
```
2026-02-19T14:02:31Z autoscaler mgr: RequestInstances(32 gpus) -> InsufficientInstanceCapacity
2026-02-19T14:03:07Z autoscaler mgr: RetryAttempt 3 -> rateLimitExceeded (Quota API)
2026-02-19T14:04:02Z runtime: pool us-west2-spot: draining 14 pods (eviction) due to preempt signals
```

platform_aaron: cloud shows spot pool eviction waves in us-west2 AZ-b, multiple customers affected. Fallback reserved capacity is tiny (3 nodes) and already saturated.

runtime_maria: current fallback policy attempted to spin up on-demand but failed due to quota and slow boot times (gpus take ~7-9m). We need immediate mitigation to stop queue from spiraling.

sre_oncall_jess: mitigation plan (immediate): 1) divert non-critical tiers to dedicated-reserved pool; 2) enable model-fallback to smaller variant for background/beta tenants; 3) throttle batch jobs / reduce max_tokens for free-tier; 4) open cloud escalation for spot capacity. Who can run the diversion?

eng_kevin: i can run diversion now. Command to re-route route-group 'gen-heavy' -> dedicated-reserved via routing policy: 
```
redwoodctl routes set --route gen-heavy --pool dedicated-reserved --policy immediate
```
I'll run it in 30s.

cs_chinedu: heads-up — two customers reported degraded latency in support tickets: ACME Corp (priority) and Shoply (beta). ACME has ongoing LLM search calls; they will see 503s. i'll notify CS to update status page.

observability-bot: Alert correlation: 12 related alerts (queue_growth, latency_p95, autoscaler_fail) — see incident timeline: https://ops.redwood/internal/incidents/1998765432

runtime_maria: additional quick mitigations: enable prefix caching on hot routes and temporary KV cache TTL extension. Also flip model fallback to 'small' for non-SLA tenants:
```
redwoodctl models fallback set --route gen-heavy --fallback small-quant --scope non-sla
```
This reduces GPU memory and may surge throughput.

sre_oncall_jess: kevin, did diversion succeed?

eng_kevin: ran the route change at 1998765470, routing now showing ~60% of gen-heavy traffic on dedicated-reserved. CPU on those nodes spiking but healthy.

platform_aaron: created cloud ticket INC-7842 with provider; requested spot replenishment and temporary on-demand allowance. ETA unknown. Also increased instance request retries and reduced instance type specificity to broaden capacity.

runtime_maria: autoscaler workaround: reduce scale step size and enable aggressive fallback to smaller instance types. patching autoscaler config now:
```
kubectl -n infra set configmap autoscaler-config --from-file=autoscaler.yaml
# set max_step=4, fallback_types=[a10g,a100-small]
```

sre_oncall_jess: we're seeing queue dropping from 120k -> 40k after routing+fallback. still some 503s for priority ACME. action item: cs_chinedu to escalate ACME SLA handoff and provide mitigation ETA.

cs_chinedu: notif sent to ACME CSM + status update published. i requested targeted warm standby in dedicated pool for ACME — awaiting confirmation.

eng_kevin: note: routing change increased cost; finance flagged but customer impact > cost. we'll re-evaluate once steady.

sre_oncall_jess: next steps: 1) keep routing in place until queue <5k and p95 latency back to normal; 2) runtime to finish autoscaler patch + enable cache; 3) platform to monitor cloud ticket and provision on-demand if provider can't recover; 4) cs to keep customers updated. I'll document actions in incident doc.

runtime_maria: autoscaler patch rolled at 1998765600. Post-patch metrics show successful smaller-instance provisioning in us-west2-A (4 nodes) but boot time ~6m. Keep route diversion for 15 more minutes.

platform_aaron: cloud responded — spot pools stabilizing slowly, but recommended on-demand fallback for critical tenants. I provisioned 6 on-demand GPUs for ACME; these show ready at 1998765680.

cs_chinedu: ACME confirmed traffic routed to warm standby; errors reduced to near-zero. they asked for postmortem and timeline.

sre_oncall_jess: good. i'm handing over to next on-call (runtime_maria) for follow-up and postmortem ownership. I'll put the detailed timeline and runbook entries in the incident doc.

runtime_maria: taking over. i'll write the postmortem draft and include recommendations: increase reserved fallback pool to 10 GPUs, adjust autoscaler to prefer on-demand when spot eviction rate >20%, add proactive cold-warm standby for top 5 customers.

incidents-bot: incident marked: mitigated -> monitoring. severity: sev2. runbook snapshot: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/gpu-eviction-fallback

sre_oncall_jess: thanks all. final notes: tag any follow-ups with #1775-fallback-capacity and assign owners. handing off now :white_check_mark:

runtime_maria: acknowledged. will ping when postmortem ready. :thumbsup:
